prompt:
Use case: real sprite animation production. Produce one transparent RGBA source sheet for this same accepted NPC: exactly6columns x3rows,18separated complete full-body poses. Request1536x1536. No labels, grid, text, scene, floor, shadow, FX, aura or particles. Each pose and every prop pixel must have generous clear alpha gutter, consistent column centers and row boot ground lines. Do not clip or touch neighboring poses. Row1 idle6, row2 talk6, row3 profession6. Row1frame1 is directional neutral calibration; one source-wide scale is measured from this neutral later. All other poses preserve physical scale; no per-pose bbox fitting. Native human standing body80px, base64x96/foot32,88; motion96x96/foot48,88 adds transparent padding only. Skull/main hair around half standing height, short torso/legs and broad crisp few-tone pixel clusters. Frame6 of each row should settle to its own directional frame1 neutral; this is a generation intent, not a claim of pixel-equal end frames.

IMAGE1 is the actual live Wang Lin Pixel02 neutral in the TARGET direction enlarged nearest8x: PRIMARY human anatomy, broad pixel treatment, material shading, camera and native scale. IMAGE2 is the SAME NPC OWNER-APPROVED Southeast motion calibration frame enlarged nearest8x (96x96 native including transparent padding, body unchanged); IMAGE3 is this SAME NPC accepted Southeast raw/motion identity source. Images2/3 support this NPC own face, skull, hair, wardrobe, physical prop hands/attachments and colors only. Reconstruct the same NPC as a true new target-direction view, never mirror/flip the Southeast image or copy Wang face/hair/wardrobe. Preserve own accepted anatomy and identity in every action; do not use another NPC as style basis.

NPC Bạch Chỉ / NPC-HN-HERBALIST. Preserve the accepted working high brown bun with leaf-green tie, tea-leaf green/ivory robe and tied practical sleeves, low compact herb basket and small jade pestle. Preserve the same adult woman face and large compact head; no new hair ornament or alternate herb tool.

ALL18poses remain NORTHWEST back-left three-quarter facing screen up-left, identical rear camera and body axes to IMAGE1. Show the back-left view throughout all18poses. Back hair, shoulders and robe dominate; do not reveal a front face, both eyes, front chest or palms through the torso. Held objects at front waist are naturally partly or fully hidden. Visible motion uses slight head inclination, shoulder/forearm changes and naturally exposed prop edges, never relocation of front-held props to the back.

Prop continuity in every row: The compact herb basket remains supported by the same physical hand as in the Southeast identity and the same jade pestle remains in the other original physical hand. Rotation changes screen projection, not hand identity. Basket contents, handle and pestle do not multiply; no free third hand holding a leaf.

Rear profession occlusion: The basket/pestle are front-held. Keep them behind the torso in North and on their natural physical side at rear quarters; show only legitimate handle/pestle edges at silhouette. The inspection nod and sleeve/wrist silhouettes can change slightly, without shifting the work gesture to the back of her body.

ROW IDLE6: frame1: Directional neutral calibration with both boots planted; frame2: Small inhalation in shoulders/cloth only; frame3: Slight sleeve/shoulder breathing change; frame4: Gentle exhalation without full-body bob or scaling; frame5: Subtle blink where eyes are actually visible, otherwise a settled shoulder/hair detail; frame6: Return to same source frame1 directional neutral.

ROW TALK6: frame1: Same directional standing neutral; frame2: Subtle speaking breath at shoulder/neck, mouth remains occluded where camera hides it; frame3: Restrained head inclination/nod, keeping the same back or back-quarter view; frame4: Small shoulder/neck speaking change while head nod begins to settle; frame5: Return head and shoulders; all low resting hands and props retained; frame6: Return to same source frame1 directional neutral.

ROW PROFESSION6: frame1: Directional standing neutral with basket and pestle low in their original physical hands; frame2: Incline head slightly to inspect the existing leaves in the held basket; frame3: Tilt the same small basket a few degrees only, retaining original contents and grip; frame4: Inspect/tilt the same small pestle with its original holding wrist just above the basket edge; never add a third item or extra hand; frame5: Settle basket/pestle to their directional neutral angles; frame6: Return to the same directional frame1 neutral.

Hair/robe/back construction is the minimal continuation of accepted identity: no extra emblems, pouches, decorations, hidden weapons, embroidery or face redesign. Motion is stationary with stable boots and genuine small pose changes; no six static duplicate images, full-body bobbing/scaling or camera rotation. Any naturally lower bounds while looking down remain natural, not normalized. New view/action is a candidate for review; owner acceptance of Southeast does not approve seven new views or runtime.
